overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific calendar notice for a Purpose 6 real-estate executive session that omitted the property, but found no violation on the other allegations.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board entered executive session under Purpose 6 on April 23 and May 9 without grounds, saying the property discussion could have been held in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Under the circumstances, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it chose to discuss the Gestalt Center in executive session under Purpose 6 on April 23 and May 9.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Purpose 6 executive session topic was insufficiently specific because the notice did not identify the property to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Having failed to do so, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law when it posted an insufficiently specific notice to the calendar on its website.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Purpose 2 executive session topic posted for May 9 was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notices were sufficiently specific as to the Purpose 2 executive sessions.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked for sanctions because the Board responded to the complaint about five months late, outside the 14-business-day window.
allegations.key_passage: Although we decline to impose sanctions for the late response, as requested by the complainant, we caution the Board to respond to any future Open Meeting Law complaints in a timely manner.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
